verses.text: Joshua the son of Nun secretly sent two men out of Shittim as spies, saying, “Go, view the land, including Jericho.” They went and came into the house of a prostitute whose name was Rahab, and slept there.
The king of Jericho was told, “Behold,  men of the children of Israel came in here tonight to spy out the land.”
Jericho’s king sent to Rahab, saying, “Bring out the men who have come to you, who have entered into your house; for they have come to spy out all the land.”
The woman took the two men and hid them. Then she said, “Yes, the men came to me, but I didn’t know where they came from.
About the time of the shutting of the gate, when it was dark, the men went out. Where the men went, I don’t know. Pursue them quickly. You may catch up with them.”
But she had brought them up to the roof, and hidden them under the stalks of flax which she had laid in order on the roof.
The men pursued them along the way to the fords of the Jordan River. As soon as those who pursued them had gone out, they shut the gate.
Before they had lain down, she came up to them on the roof.
She said to the men, “I know that Yahweh has given you the land, and that the fear of you has fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land melt away before you.

For we have heard how Yahweh dried up the water of the Red Sea before you, when you came out of Egypt; and what you did to the two kings of the Amorites, who were beyond the Jordan, to Sihon and to Og, whom you utterly destroyed.
As soon as we had heard it, our hearts melted, and there wasn’t any more spirit in any man, because of you: for Yahweh your God, he is God in heaven above, and on earth beneath.
Now therefore, please swear to me by Yahweh, since I have dealt kindly with you, that you also will deal kindly with my father’s house, and give me a true sign;
and that you will save alive my father, my mother, my brothers, and my sisters, and all that they have, and will deliver our lives from death.”
The men said to her, “Our life for yours, if you don’t talk about this business of ours; and it shall be, when Yahweh gives us the land, that we will deal kindly and truly with you.”
Then she let them down by a cord through the window; for her house was on the side of the wall, and she lived on the wall.
She said to them, “Go to the mountain, lest the pursuers find you. Hide yourselves there three days, until the pursuers have returned. Afterward, you may go your way.”
The men said to her, “We will be guiltless of this your oath which you’ve made us to swear.

Behold, when we come into the land, tie this line of scarlet thread in the window which you used to let us down. Gather to yourself into the house your father, your mother, your brothers, and all your father’s household.

It shall be that whoever goes out of the doors of your house into the street, his blood will be on his head, and we will be guiltless. Whoever is with you in the house, his blood shall be on our head, if any hand is on him.
But if you talk about this business of ours, then we shall be guiltless of your oath which you’ve made us to swear.”
She said, “Let it be as you have said.” She sent them away, and they departed. Then she tied the scarlet line in the window.
They went, and came to the mountain, and stayed there three days, until the pursuers had returned. The pursuers sought them all along the way, but didn’t find them.
Then the two men returned, descended from the mountain, crossed the river, and came to Joshua the son of Nun. They told him all that had happened to them.
They said to Joshua, “Truly Yahweh has delivered all the land into our hands. Moreover, all the inhabitants of the land melt away before us.”

footnotes.content: Joshua sends spies out from Shittim in secret—the first step into the promised land is reconnaissance, not the trumpet blast we might expect. Two men slip away quietly to view Jericho, and they end up in the house of a woman named Rahab. Sometimes the Lord uses the most unlikely doors to work His purpose.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The king hears of the spies at once—the enemy is watching, alert for any sign of invasion. Yet the Lord already knows this too, and it changes nothing of His plan. We tend to panic when our moves are noticed; the Lord calmly moves forward regardless.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The king demands Rahab produce the spies. This is the moment where her choice hardens: she can hand them over, or she can lie and shield them. She chooses to protect the strangers at real risk to herself—a choice that matters to the Lord, whatever her station or past.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rahab's lie—"Yes, they came, but I don't know where they went"—saves the lives of two men sent by the Lord. She acts as a shield in that moment, making a choice for mercy over the king's authority. The text doesn't condemn her untruth; it records her faithfulness to the Lord over the kingdom of Jericho.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: She sends the king's men after imaginary fugitives heading toward the Jordan—her words turn their pursuit away from the roof where the spies are hidden. A quick lie, born of courage, and the hunters chase a phantom while the real quarry stays safe overhead.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Flax stalks on a roof in ancient Jericho—arranged in order for drying, they become the perfect cover. How often the Lord uses the ordinary work of a woman's hands to hide His servants. The tools of her trade become the tools of His providence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The pursuers race along the Jordan road while the gate of Jericho shuts behind them. Even this detail is the Lord's hand: they chase the wrong direction, and the city's gate closes—cutting off any route back quickly. Every element serves His purpose.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Before the spies can rest, Rahab climbs to the roof to meet them. She has sent the hunters away, and now she comes to speak truth. No weariness stops her; the moment demands her word, and she gives it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rahab declares her faith aloud: "I know Yahweh has given you the land." She has heard of His works across the desert, and her heart has already accepted what her city refuses to believe. Her confession echoes what Israel itself will learn over the years ahead—that the Lord is God, and His word is certain.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Red Sea, Sihon, Og—Rahab knows the story of what the Lord has done. News travels, and her city's fear is not idle; it is rooted in witness to His mighty hand. Sometimes faith in a stranger's God starts not with doctrine, but with memory of His power.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in Rahab's words: she declares that Yahweh is God in heaven and on earth—a confession that resonates across the centuries. Long before the theologian, she knows what matters most. Her fear of the Lord has turned her courage into faith.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rahab asks for an oath: "Since I have dealt kindly with you, deal kindly with my father's house." She binds herself to the spies' word, trading her loyalty for their protection of her family. It is a bold transaction—her life and theirs, weighed in a covenant.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: She names them one by one: father, mother, brothers, sisters, and all that belongs to them. She is not thinking of herself alone; she is thinking of her whole house, bound together by blood and roof. Her request is specific and tender—she will not leave anyone behind.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The spies swear to her: "Our life for yours if you keep our secret." They pledge their own lives as collateral—a grave oath that binds them to protect her when the moment comes. The Lord honors such oaths; they are threads that bind His people to one another.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A cord through the window, a house on the wall—the geography of Jericho becomes her escape route. What once housed her as a woman of the city now becomes her passage out of it. The Lord uses the very walls she lived within to set her free.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: She advises them: hide in the mountain three days until the pursuers return, then go your way. Her counsel is practical and wise—she knows her city's rhythms and how long the search will last. A woman who knows her place also knows how to help strangers leave it safely.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The spies answer carefully: "We will be guiltless of your oath if you break silence about this." They set one condition—her silence is the seal. They have sworn to protect her house, but only if the secret stays hidden.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A scarlet thread in the window—when they return to take the land, this sign will mark her house for deliverance, just as the blood on the doorposts marked the houses of Israel in Egypt. One color, one thread, one covenant: she will be remembered.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The spies set a boundary: anyone inside the house will be saved; anyone outside bears the consequence. It is stern and clear—they call Rahab to gather her household together and stay within. Stay inside the covenant, they are saying, and you will live.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: If she betrays them, their oath is void—a final warning spoken as they prepare to leave. Her silence is not asked lightly; it is the price of all that has been promised. She must choose between her city and the spies, between the king and the covenant.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rahab accepts their word—"Let it be as you have said"—and ties the scarlet thread in her window. The sign is visible; the covenant is sealed. She has staked everything on the word of two strangers and the God she has come to trust.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The spies reach the mountain and wait three days while their pursuers search the roads and find nothing. Time passes; the hunters give up. The Lord's hand protects them in that hiding place, and their faith in Rahab's word proves true.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They return to Joshua with all that has happened—the rescue, the oath, the scarlet thread, the promise that the land will be delivered into their hands. What began as a covert mission becomes a testimony to what the Lord has already prepared in the hearts of His future subjects.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They report to Joshua: "Truly Yahweh has delivered all the land into our hands." The spies have seen the Lord's work not in a supernatural sign, but in the faith of a woman who believed Him and acted. The greatest victories are often announced through human courage.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
